explanation: The Dijon article opens its § Prelude with the claim: "After the French defeats at Novara (6 June) and Guinegatte (16 August), Louis XII anticipated a counter-attack by the Imperial armies on France’s own soil." Novara is the defeat that emptied Italy of the French army — la Trémoille was recalled from Italy to govern Dijon — and the invasion of Burgundy came three months later. `enabled` and not `caused`: the article says the defeat opened France to a counter-attack, not that it made this siege inevitable. Probable: Wikipedia alone, and the sentence carries no citation of its own.
